newsitem.title: USA: SEC's Maco warns on municipal bond lawyer hiring.
newsitem.headline: SEC's Maco warns on municipal bond lawyer hiring.

text.p: A top SEC official warned states and localities on Friday not to hire municipal bond lawyers and financial advisers who think that the disclosure provisions of the federal securities laws do not apply to their clients.

"There are still a few bond counsel and financial advisers who are in denial as to the applicability of the federal securities laws" to issuers of tax-exempt bonds, Paul Maco, director of the Securities and Exchange Commission's office of municipal securities, said. "You may want to know if you've retained one before you rely on their advice."

The federal securities laws require all securities issuers, including states and localities issuing muni bonds, to make sure their disclosure documents do not have misstatements or omit "material" facts.

The SEC has beefed up enforcement in the muni arena. It has taken enforcement actions since 1996 involving the adequacy of disclosure in bond offerings by Orange County, Calif., and Maricopa County, Ariz.
Some bond professionals contend, however, that SEC has gone overboard in regulating the muni market, including its release of tough disclosure standards in November 1994 for bond issuers.

Maco said on Friday, "Issuers should insist that any persons retained to assist in preparation of disclosure documents have a professional understanding of the disclosure requirements under the federal securities laws."

He noted that a recent "pocket guide" on disclosure issued by municipal groups urges localities to understand clearly the responsibilities of all parties to a bond deal, including the professionals they hire.

"Don't put yourself in the position, for example, where you think your bond counsel is giving you disclosure advise and they think thay are only providing you with" tax opinions on the bonds, said Maco, who was speaking before a Government Finance Officers Association group in Albany, N.Y.
